_arch_note_0215: CODEBOOK / DICTIONARY READOUT (task b8319718). NEW cell_mode='codebook' on LightMHL. Geometry differs from 0207 only in tph (64->48): H=8, tph=48, nap=8, d_in=d_out=48, full-rank compress (H*d_in=384=d_model), read_top_n=1, pair-difference addressing, margin confidence, no z_norm. So T = H*tph = 384 tables, 2^nap=256 cells each. THE READOUT: each addressed cell stores a single SCALAR w_c (r=1), NOT a d_out vector -> cell store shape (n_tables=384, 256, 1). Per table t the coefficient g_t = s_t * w_{c_t} (s_t the existing margin-confidence score, c_t the addressed cell); NO sum across tables/heads. Concatenate all T=384 coefficients into g in R^384, then decode with ONE shared matrix per layer M in R^{d_model x T} = R^{384x384}: y = M*g = sum_t g_t * M[:,t]. This REPLACES the usual per-head gather-and-sum readout + decompress (decompress is Identity; M lives in LightMHL). No bias. M init std 0.02, scalar store w_c small (~initial_weights_noise) so the arm starts y~0 (well-behaved). CONSTANT-mode path stays bit-exact (guarded); all lutorch regression tests pass. FLOPs/token/layer ~= compress 147,456 + decoder M 147,456 + negligible addressing ~= 295k MACs, ~4x under vanilla FFN's 1,179,648 MACs. Params/layer ~= scalar store 98,304 + M 147,456 + W_compress 147,456+bias ~= 393k. IDEA: a big cheap codebook of scalars (lots of stored capacity, near-zero FLOPs) + one small learned decode dictionary -- capacity in the store, compute in M. Compare vs 0207 constant (1.131286), margin_readout 0214 (in progress), gated_affine 0213 (1.128507), dense@48K (1.115420, sigma=0.00335).
